Sentence (English): We had a Whirlpool that worked great but lasted only 5 1/2 years (6 months after expiration of the extended warranty! ).
Comments (English): [ Disappointing and will be returning ] || ---------------- || We had a Whirlpool that worked great but lasted only 5 1/2 years (6 months after expiration of the extended warranty! ). Cost of repair was $300-$400 so decided to shop and "upgrade" to a Bosch after some research. Costco ordering, delivery and install were a snap. But first time using two things jumped out: (1) the tines are spaced way too close together and (2) no light showing you the cycle is complete . On the first issue, the unit is the standard 24" model but it sure does seem to hold less dishes than any DW we've owned. It's very plate-friendly, but forget bowls, glasses and cups (or odd objects). The tines are not adjustable. So if you're having a dinner party where you use nothing but plates, this is the DW for you! Otherwise, not so much. Second, the lack of an exterior light may seem minor but it's not. For a company that markets how quiet their unit is, and it is (but not noticeably quieter than the Whirlpool we had), there is no way to tell when the cycle is finished. We usually run our DWs overnight on a delay feature, so that's not much of an issue, but in the daytime if you need to run several washes, you're left guessing. What a remarkable engineering oversight! Some other minor issues: other than a very basic "quick start guide" you have to go to Bosch website and download the operating manual. Not ideal. I note the guide has "suggested loading patterns" with pictures. Ironically, I think these pictures bolster my observation. They have some bowls, but very few, and the ones they have appear to be shallower, at least compared to what we have. Cleaning, quietness etc. are both very good. But the lack of space and inability to adjust the tines that were designed way too close are why we are returning this model product.

For a company that markets how quiet their unit is, and it is (but not noticeably quieter than the Whirlpool we had), there is no way to tell when the cycle is finished. We usually run our DWs overnight on a delay feature, so that's not much of an issue, but in the daytime if you need to run several washes, you're left guessing. What a remarkable engineering oversight! Some other minor issues: other than a very basic 'quick start guide'  you have to go to Bosch website and download the operating manual. Not ideal. I note the guide has 'suggested loading patterns' with pictures. Ironically, I think these pictures bolster my observation. They have some bowls, but very few, and the ones they have appear to be shallower, at least compared to what we have. Cleaning, quietness etc. are both very good. But the lack of space and inability to adjust the tines that were designed way too close are why we are returning this model  product.

Sentence (English): This unit replaces a Kitchenaid whose motor died after only 7 years and was too expensive to repair.
Comments (English): [ Pleasantly surprised ] || ---------------- || This unit replaces a Kitchenaid whose motor died after only 7 years and was too expensive to repair. This unit is not as quiet (50 vs 47 db, probably because the May tag has less than half the insulating material), and has only 2 lower wash arms rather than 4 on the Kitchenaid. But Consumer Reports rated the wash performance as Very Good, so we took a chance on the May tag because it was $150 less than the comparable Kitchen aid. It was a good decision. The Maytag is still pretty quiet. And the dishes come out very clean. The top rack is designed differently from past dishwashers, but actually allows for more flexibility in loading, so we actually like it better; and the top rack, while not adjustable, is lower than we have had, allowing us to put some larger items on top that we could not before, but there is still plenty of height for the lower rack. We got this unit because of the hard food disposer (less pre rinsing required) and the leak detection feature (it was an undetected leak that ruined the motor in our Kitchenaid), and it was the least expensive if the 4 units we were considering. Overall it is a fine machine. The one con: no parts list. Not even from the Maytag website or any parts website. So finding replacement parts is a little more problematic.

Things to note are that I feel like the machine has less capacity available than you would think and you definitely need to use rinse aid to dry glass well since there is no heating element to dry dishes. Most important of all for installation the Bosch requires a outlet for power. It is not setup for hardwired installation from factory and you will be at the mercy of the installer if they have the part available that is required. Because of the few negatives I wasn't aware of I would rate it a 4. If you know ahead of time you will be completely satisfied with this dishwasher.

Therefore, if I want to put anything larger than saucer and very small glasses in the middle rack, I have to remove the third, upper rack, which I did. So, there is no more room in this one than the older models, and unless one has lots of small dishes, the third, upper rack will likely not be of use. I still love the brand.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher beginning of January 2023 from Samsung.com, and in the last 6 months we have had nothing but issues with it.
Comments (English): [ Super Disapointed with Quality and Samsung Support ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher beginning of January 2023 from Samsung.com, and in the last 6 months we have had nothing but issues with it. The original delivery was rescheduled 3 times, "so glad" I stayed home from work the first two scheduled times just to get an update mid way through the day that the delivery will be rescheduled. Once the dishwasher was finally delivered, within 30 days, the ball-brings from the second shelf literally fell apart in the inside the dishwasher. It took 1 week for the technician to come out and another 2 weeks for the parts to arrive - so 3 weeks without a dishwasher. Couple of months later, the middle spray arm literally fell off inside the dishwasher. Now we come to the 6 months since purchase, and dishwasher is leaking all over the floor. After spending almost an hour with the Samsung support staff on the phone, the best they can do is send the technician out 9 days from today so s/he can verify that there is an issue before a replacement can be ordered. I am making a bet that I will be once again without a dishwasher for 3-4 weeks. The quality of this product is terrible and if you are thinking that Samsung will take care of you if you have issues, re-think it - Samsung relies exclusively on 3rd party support centers after 15 days of purchase and the 3rd party availability is limited and if you try to call them, it is impossible to get someone to answer the phone. I even asked the Samsung rep to call them and after multiple attempts they achieved the same result as I did (no answer). Samsung, I expected better quality and better service coming from you and now I think this will be the last Samsung product I buy.

Sentence (English): Tl;dr If you're going to spend this much money on a dishwasher, buy a Miele - you'll end up saving money.
Comments (English): [ Buy a Miele ] || ---------------- || Tl;dr If you're going to spend this much money on a dishwasher, buy a Miele - you'll end up saving money.Our beloved Miele Inspira series dishwasher died after nearly 20 years of daily use. At the time, Miele was having supply chain issues due to the silicon shortage. So we went with the Bosch 500 series thinking, although it wouldn't be at Miele quality - it would at least last a decent amount, right? Wrong.Everything was going great until about 10 months after we bought the dishwasher, it generated an error: E:02 (heater relay fault). After rebooting the machine to clear the error code, I was thinking it may have been a build up of lime scale in the heater core, so I ran Bosch descaler through it.Mid cycle the dishwasher fully bricked itself - entirely unresponsive. Which tells me the motherboard and the boards downstream from it are probably toast.Like I said at the top of this review, if you're already shopping this price point: buy a Miele and avoid the headache.

Sentence (English): I'm devastated that we spent $900 for what we thought would be a premium appliance for our family of 6.
Comments (English): [ Couldn't be more disappointed ] || ---------------- || I'm devastated that we spent $900 for what we thought would be a premium appliance for our family of 6. I have little kids and we have stainless lunchboxes that just don't have a place in that dishwasher. They fit just fine in our very old KitchenAid, which I miss dearly and regret not fixing instead of "upgrading" to this horrible appliance. I am so angry that I can't return it and wasted so much money on this.

Sentence (English): I had the pocket handle version of this same washer 3 years before it had an out of warranty pump failure.
Comments (English): [ Great three rack dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I had the pocket handle version of this same washer 3 years before it had an out of warranty pump failure. Even though it stopped working way sooner than i planned I liked the dishwasher so much I bought it again without hesitation. It is quiet and cleans even super dirty dishes every day. This is the only dishwasher that I know of with a third rack that is not just for flatware and flat items. It will accommodate small cups and bowls and glass sandwich containers in addition to lids, measuring cups, tongs, etc. the lower rack is spacious and well laid out and has a flatware basket. The middle rack is adjustable - i have it raised all the way so large items can go in the bottom but even then the right side of the top still accommodates large stadium cups, tervis cups and yeti coffee travel mugs. The left side still holds other cups just not tall ones as the left side of third rack takes up a little of the clearance room so that it can hold cups, etc. I don't use the dry cycle and just run added sani rinse. Everything comes out dry except for plastic items collect a little water. That's an easy trade off to having a very quiet and efficient dishwasher.

This model is far easier to load than the last Bosch that we'd bought only a couple of years ago. It promised a short cycle but the installer recommended against using it, except maybe during s party, because of the extra stress this cycle put on the machine. The Bosch we had before the last one - bought about 15 years ago - had a short cycle that wprked very well and the washer was still working well 9 years later when we sold that condo. It is quiet so the 2 hour 20 minute cycle is OK. We have an open plan living/dining area so a noisy dishwasher would not be welcome. We scrape our dishes and rinse them before loading them. So faar, three months later, everything has come out clean and streak free. I suspect the limitations on short cycles derive from the EPA/DOE regulations on water usage and detergent formulation so I don't blame Bosch for the limitation on short cycles. I'd recommend this model. It is not the most expensive or quietest Bosch model - but a good compromise between price and performance.

Sentence (English): First off this dishwash is near silent and you really only know it run is from either the red light on the floor or when it is draining water.
Comments (English): [ Extremely Quiet but door is flimsy ] || ---------------- || First off this dishwash is near silent and you really only know it run is from either the red light on the floor or when it is draining water. That said it clean dish very well and does a great job of drying them. There is always some cup that have a very concave bottom that will still have some drips of water, but I see no issue with that. The con is the build. Everything is super light weight and feels cheap. The top aka 3rd drawer is not smooth to open and close. All other drawers middle and bottom are perfectly fine, but when they are empy it lack that premium weight feel. The front door on the hand I feel would break if a small child climbed up on it or it was bumped into. You can literally feel the door twist and flex. Yes I know I bought the 100 series, but the front door bugs me. Will I return it, no, but I feel like I have to take extra caution around it. If the dishwasher last for a long time, then I'll consider it a non-issue. As for installation, I was really fearful of this because I saw so many bad reviews of one company doing delivery and another doing install. Seems like in my area it is just one company that does both, which is how it should be. They installed it in under 15mins and did another 15-20mins of testing. They found a few areas of possible leaks for me to lookout for as some of my existing hoses were just old. They left paper under the area and showed me where to check for leak and what might need to be replaced. After 48hrs of looking for leaks I never found any, but I do appreciate their transparency. I guess I'm one of the lucky few that had a positive delivery experience.

Sentence (English): This unit replaced a GE Cafe dishwasher that, in comparison, was apparently never very good and had degraded to terrible at the end.
Comments (English): [ So clean. and so quiet. ] || ---------------- || This unit replaced a GE Cafe dishwasher that, in comparison, was apparently never very good and had degraded to terrible at the end. This one cleans anything, dries most things perfectly, and is super silent doing it (the noisiest part of the whole process is the fill valve adding water). The other surprise is how much it holds. We haven't cooked a meal yet where everything didn't fit in one load; including pots and pans! I definitely helps having all the silverware up and out of the way on the top drawer. Negatives? It might have been Lowe's website error, but it did not come with the top silverware tray/drawer in the pictures. It came with a useless shallow tray for… something. That was super disappointing. I ended up paying another $80 to get the silverware rack from Bosh parts. Glad I did - silverware comes out perfect - but sucks I had to pay extra. My only other complaint is that the touchpad is a tad touch resistant: sometimes it takes 5-6 presses to get a button to register.

Sentence (English): I had been half-heartedly looking for a dishwasher since last Summer when my 13 year old Kenmore decided to retire.
Comments (English): [ Love This Quiet Beast! ] || ---------------- || I had been half-heartedly looking for a dishwasher since last Summer when my 13 year old Kenmore decided to retire. From KitchenAid to LG to Miele I read about them all, and after looking at the "Consumer's" quality review magazines there was no question I wanted a Bosch. I was looking at models at big box competitors, but then I received the new Costco email announcing they now carried Bosch dishwashers. I ordered the Bosch from Costco, it was delivered in five days, then installed the following day. From the delivery to the install, everything went smooth and easy. The installer said he had the same model at his home, but he paid $150 more for his and it didn't include installation. This dishwasher cleans the nastiest dishes until they're sparkling, then rinses them with a super high heat rinse and shuts off. There's no heating element in this dishwasher, and that high heat rinse cycle actually dries the dishes. This dishwasher is so quiet it projects a small red light onto the floor so you know it's running…!

Sentence (English): Large capacity, several functions, pleasant little music without being too intense to announce the end of the cycle.
Comments (English): [ Worn baskets and locks to be reworked ] || ---------------- || Large capacity, several functions, pleasant little music without being too intense to announce the end of the cycle. Disappointment for the quality of the baskets. I had to have a basket changed because of a rust problem at the end of the first year of use (this was covered by the warranty). I have to change the same basket again, but this time the warranty is over. The top basket also has a little rust, but it's not as bothersome because it's a small hole in the material. I never put a knife/sharp dishes/metal in it, no idea what's causing the problem. ** Small downside for the control lock function. All buttons are locked EXCEPT the "power" button. If you have a young child who likes to touch buttons that make music and lights, wash cycles are easily stopped. It might be interesting if the lock function locks ALL functions.
Comments (Original): [ Paniers usées et verrouillage à retravailler ] || ---------------- || Grande capacité, plusieurs fonctions, petite musique agréable sans être trop intense pour annoncer la fin du cycle. Déception pour la qualité des paniers. J'ai dû faire changer un panier à cause d'un problème de rouille à la fin de la 1ere année d'utilisation (c'était couvert par la garantie).  Je dois de nouveau faire changer le même panier, mais cette fois la garantie est finie.  Le panier du haut à aussi un peu de rouille, mais ce n'est pas aussi dérangeant car c'est un petit trou dans le matériau.  Je m'y mets jamais de couteau/vaisselle tranchante/métal, aucune idée de la cause du problème. ** Petit bémol pour la fonction de verrouillage des commandes.  Tous les boutons sont verrouillés SAUF le bouton 'power'.  Si vous avez un jeune enfant qui aime toucher à des boutons qui font de la musique et de la lumière, les cycles de lavage sont facilement arrêtés... Ce pourrait être intéressant que la fonction verrouillage verrouille TOUTES les fonctions.

Disappointment for the quality of the baskets. I had to have a basket changed because of a rust problem at the end of the first year of use (this was covered by the warranty). I have to have the same basket changed again, but this time the warranty is over. The top basket also has a little rust, but it's not as bothersome because it's a small hole in the material. I never put a knife/sharp tableware/metal in it, no idea what's causing the problem. ** Small downside for the control lock function. All buttons are locked EXCEPT the "power" button. If you have a young child who likes to touch buttons that play music and lights, wash cycles are easily stopped. It might be interesting if the lock function locks ALL functions.
Comments (Original): [ Paniers usées et verrouillage à retravailler ] || ---------------- || Grande capacité, plusieurs fonctions, petite musique agréable sans être trop intense pour annoncer la fin du cycle. Déception pour la qualité des paniers. J'ai dû faire changer un panier à cause d'un problème de rouille à la fin de la 1ere année d'utilisation (c'était couvert par la garantie).  Je dois de nouveau faire changer le même panier, mais cette fois la garantie est finie.  Le panier du haut à aussi un peu de rouille, mais ce n'est pas aussi dérangeant car c'est un petit trou dans le matériau.  Je m'y mets jamais de couteau/vaisselle tranchante/métal, aucune idée de la cause du problème. ** Petit bémol pour la fonction de verrouillage des commandes.  Tous les boutons sont verrouillés SAUF le bouton 'power'.  Si vous avez un jeune enfant qui aime toucher à des boutons qui font de la musique et de la lumière, les cycles de lavage sont facilement arrêtés... Ce pourrait être intéressant que la fonction verrouillage verrouille TOUTES les fonctions.

Sentence (English): Just bought a Samsung refrigerator .
Comments (English): [ Does Not Filter Out Many Chemicals!  ] || ---------------- || Just bought a Samsung refrigerator . Ran over a gallon of water through the system. I tested the water from the fridge and got 154 PPM. I tested the water from the tap and it was 171 PPM. Apparently it doesn't filter out a lot of chemicals. I had a Zero Water that I discarded because the fridge had a filter. That was a mistake. There is no listing of the filter's efficacy. I wonder why! Will have to install a filtration system prior to connecting to the fridge.

Sentence (English): I had been half-heartedly looking for a dishwasher since last Summer when my 13 year old Kenmore decided to retire.
Comments (English): [ Love This Quiet Beast! ] || ---------------- || I had been half-heartedly looking for a dishwasher since last Summer when my 13 year old Kenmore decided to retire. From KitchenAid to LG to Miele I read about them all, and after looking at the “Consumer's” quality review magazines there was no question I wanted a Bosch. I was looking at models at big box competitors, but then I received the new Costco email announcing they now carried Bosch dishwashers. I ordered the Bosch from Costco, it was delivered in five days, then installed the following day. From the delivery to the install, everything went smooth and easy. The installer said he had the same model at his home, but he paid $150 more for his and it didn't include installation. This dishwasher cleans the nastiest dishes until they're sparkling, then rinses them with a super high heat rinse and shuts off. There's no heating element in this dishwasher, and that high heat rinse cycle actually dries the dishes. This dishwasher is so quiet it projects a small red light onto the floor so you know it's running…!

Sentence (English): We had a 2009 bosh dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Build quality not what it was 13 years ago. ] || ---------------- || We had a 2009 bosh dishwasher. It is a wonderful dishwasher, the build quality is excellent, cleans dishes excellently, easy to operate and extremely silent. We remodeled our kitchen and went with stainless steel finishes, unfortunately our dishwasher was white. No problem, just purchase a 2023 bosch dishwasher of the same series. Unfortunately bosh is not what it used to be! The new bosch dishwasher build quality is very cheap and fragile, the buttons and racks feel very cheap and that they will break well before 10 years. The buttons feel very fragile. The sound insulation has been reduced, the dishwasher is significantly louder (maybe the 800 series is better build quality). The addition of the start button is an unnecessary complication of operation, push the on/off button, push the wash mode, push options, push start now quick you only have 3 seconds to close the door or the dishwasher will reset. We often use the delay option so the dishwasher runs overnight. If you open the door to add dishes while the dishwasher is in this delay and you leave the door open for more than 4 seconds the dishwasher resets no indication of this, you just have dirty dishes the next morning. My advice is if you have an old bosch dishwasher, keep it and just get it repaired. The new ones are a disappointment!

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher with as part of a 4pc set and had it professionally installed in our newly constructed home.
Comments (English): [ Pump failure at 3.5 years ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher with as part of a 4pc set and had it professionally installed in our newly constructed home. In the first year it over flowed and spilled water on our new hardwood floors twice. We assumed it was our fault that the dishes weren't clean enough and food debris was the cause. Next, it doesn't dry the dishes very well at all. We use rinse aid as required but dishes still come out wet. We have to have to hand dry them before they can be put away. Last month there was smoke and an electrical smell coming from the bottom front panel and it wouldn't drain. We called LG and they told me a technician would be in touch. After 3 weeks of back and forth a technician finally came out and made the repairs. To LGs credit the part and labor was covered. However the experience to get the repair made was terrible. The other appliances have been fine, but these are the last LG appliances we will own.

Sentence (English): Full disclosure: we bought the WDP730 in the warehouse.
Comments (English): [ No Pre-Rinsing Needed, Quite, Awesome ] || ---------------- || Full disclosure: we bought the WDP730 in the warehouse. No delivery, no setup. The P model has a "Pocket" handle vs the "Towel bar" handle model here. Otherwise, they are identical. With this washer, we just scrape and leave the dishes, pots and pans in until late night when we start the cycle. We're using Kirkland pods with just the "Normal" setting without either "Heat Dry" or "Extended Dry". Next morning, everything is perfectly clean, dry and spotless. (For best results use common sense and avoid situations where water can pool like the bottom of glasses and mugs. Also empty it from bottom to top so that whatever does pool on the upper shelves doesn't wet what's below.) Did I mention that my daughter is under the influence of the Great British Bake Off? Mixing bowls, utensils, cake pans, etc. go in with just a scraping and come out clean. Again use common sense: it's not going to clean a 1/4" thick layer of sponge cake off, but if there's a thin coating like what remains after scraping, it will clean it without any rinsing. (Kudos to the Kirkland pods.) Noise? It sounds like there's a table-top fountain in the kitchen. Yeah, ya know? The kind people buy for the pleasant sound of gently flowing water. My one complaint is with the instruction manual which is pretty useless and intended for several different models. If it's available on-line, I couldn't find it. About the only actionable information is the table explain the various cycles. (As I said, we use "Normal" exclusively and no extra drying.) And the installation manual ain't that great either. If you live in the Southwest this machine is perfect since you really don't have to waste ANY water rinsing stuff off before it goes in.

Sentence (English): We previously owned a Jenn-Air/Whirlpool for 10 years.
Comments (English): [ Mixed feelings ] || ---------------- || We previously owned a Jenn-Air/Whirlpool for 10 years. We transitioned to Bosch based on reviews and independent stores telling us how the quality is the best in the industry. Right away, we were disappointed. 1. It is noisy. Our old dishwasher was rated a 40, this one a 42. I had no idea how much impact 2 decibels would make. Is Bosch SURE it's rated at 42? Was Jenn-Air better than 40? 2. The door is flimsy and flexes. When we open using any area on the handle other then dead center, it's visible how much the door rotates. 3. The stainless steel front piece is impossible to keep clean. It's obviously not as good of quality as our JennWhirl. 4. The loading pattern is awful. I recognize it will take time to get used to the new racks, but we can only fit one large item on the bottom because the tines are too close together. We've figured out large items fit better on the top, but it's still less capacity than what we had before.I wonder if it would have made a difference to bump up to the next better series of Bosch? Either way, I sure hope I don't have to find out before 10 years are up because that's how long I expect this dishwasher to last given all of the hype.
